rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghuthāʾ is debris carried by a flood, such as dried plants, leaves, and worn branches; the word may have a doubled thāʾ.
rows.anchor: والغثاء بضم الغين وربما شددت الثاء ما يحمله السيل من يابس النبات والورق والعيدان البالية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer that the wrongdoers be distanced is a curse, a denunciation, or a supplication against them.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فبعدا للقوم الظالمين } إبعاد ولعن لهم أو دعاء عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unnamed people destroyed by the cry may have been Thamud, the people of Salih, since scripture places them after Noah's people and says they were destroyed by a cry.
rows.anchor: وليس من البعيد أن يكونوا هم ثمود قوم صالح عليه السلام فقد ذكر الله سبحانه في قصتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tatrā describes messengers or groups arriving successively, one after another, individually.
rows.anchor: يقال جاءوا تترى أي فرادى يتبع بعضهم بعضا، ومنه التواتر وهو تتابع الشيء وترا وفرادى،

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī explains wātartu al-khabar as sending reports one after another with a short interval between them.
rows.anchor: وعن الأصمعي واترت الخبر أتبعت بعضه بعضا وبين الخبرين هنيهة انتهى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second thumma marks progression in the account rather than elapsed time; the passage summarizes prophets between Noah's people and Moses' people.
rows.anchor: و { ثم } للتراخي بحسب الذكر دون الزمان، والقصة إجمال منتزع من قصص الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the people destroyed by the cry, God created later generations and sent successive messengers; each community rejected its messenger, so the communities followed one another in destruction.
rows.anchor: وأرسلنا إليهم رسلنا متتابعين يتبع بعضهم بعضا كلما جاء أمة رسولها المبعوث منها إليها كذبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the destroyed communities into tales after they had been real beings leaving traces, and the passage ends by invoking distance for unbelieving people.
rows.anchor: وجعلناهم أحاديث أي صيرناهم قصصا وأخبارا بعد ما كانوا أعيانا ذوات آثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses describe God's recurring practice: successive generations are tested through messengers, reject them, and then face divine recompense through destruction.
rows.anchor: والآيات تدل على أنه كان من سنة الله إنشاء قرن بعد قرن وهدايتهم إلى الحق بإرسال رسول بعد رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them mere reports vividly expresses divine overpowering: God erases the enemies of truth and their traces, leaving only news of them.
rows.anchor: أبلغ كلمة تفصح عن القهر الإلهي الذي يغشى أعداء الحق والمكذبين لدعوته حيث يمحو العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' signs include the staff, the shining hand, and the other signs shown to Pharaoh and his people; clear authority means a clear proof.
rows.anchor: الآيات هي العصا واليد البيضاء وسائر الآيات التي أراها موسى فرعون وقومه، والسلطان المبين الحجة الواضحة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects interpreting the clear authority specifically as Moses' staff.
rows.anchor: وتفسير بعضهم السلطان بالعصا غير سديد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some explain that Pharaoh's chiefs are singled out because they were the nobles whom the rest of the people followed.
rows.anchor: قيل إنما ذكر ملأ فرعون واكتفى بهم عن ذكر قومه لأنهم الأشراف المتبوعون وسائر القوم أتباع يتبعونهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were 'high' because they dominated and enslaved others, especially the Children of Israel; elevation on earth figuratively means ruling people by coercion.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكونهم عالين أنهم كانوا يعلون على غيرهم فيستعبدونهم كما علوا على بني إسرائيل واستعبدوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By calling Moses and Aaron ordinary men, Pharaoh's people deny that the brothers have superiority; they regard their own mastery over the brothers' people as proof of their own rank.
rows.anchor: المراد بكونهما بشرين مثلهم نفي أن يكون لهما فضل عليهم، وبكون قومهما لهم عابدين فضلهم عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reasoning implies that Moses should worship them rather than ask them to believe, as Pharaoh's threat to imprison Moses also illustrates.
rows.anchor: كما قال فرعون لموسى { لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's people were destroyed; the book was given so the Children of Israel might be guided, since the Torah came after Pharaoh and his chiefs perished.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم بنو إسرائيل لأن التوراة إنما نزلت بعد هلاك فرعون وملائه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the whole believing community, the slander was beneficial because it exposed corrupt members and prompted reform; revelation also warned a religious community about neglected duties.
rows.anchor: أن المجتمع الصالح من سعادته أن يتميز فيه أهل الزيغ والفساد ليكونوا على بصيرة من أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following statement that each person bears the sin he acquired supports the general address: the slanderers became exposed by their own guilt instead of exposing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فظاهر الجملة أن أهل الإفك الجائين به يعرفون بإثمه ويتميزون به عندكم فيفتضحون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the view that the episode benefited only the accused because they would be rewarded while the slanderers sinned; that reading wrongly limits the address to the accused.
rows.anchor: وأما قول من قال إن المراد بكونه خيرا لهم أنهم يثابون بما اتهموهم بالإفك

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators take the one who took the greater share to mean the person who assumed the main part of the slander and persisted in spreading it.
rows.anchor: فسروا كبره بمعنى معظمه والضمير للإفك، والمعنى والذي تولى معظم الإفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reproaches listeners for failing to reject the rumor immediately and to think well of the person accused.
rows.anchor: توبيخ لهم إذ لم يردوا الحديث حينما سمعوه ولم يظنوا بمن رمي به خيرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'of themselves' replaces an expected 'you'; it points to faith as a natural restraint and grounds the duty to think well of fellow believers.
rows.anchor: من وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر، والأصل " ظننتم بأنفسكم " والوجه في تبديل الضمير وصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are one self through faith and its consequences, so they should assume good of one another and avoid speaking without knowledge.
rows.anchor: فإنهم جميعا كنفس واحدة في التلبس بالإيمان ولوازمه وآثاره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers should have called the report manifest slander: a claim without knowledge or proof is legally judged false whether or not it is true in reality.
rows.anchor: لأن الخبر الذي لا علم لمخبره به والدعوى التي لا بينة لمدعيها عليها محكوم شرعا بالكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true accusation would have been supported by four witnesses; without them, the accusers are legally judged liars because an unproven claim is false testimony.
rows.anchor: فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فهم محكومون شرعا بالكذب لأن الدعوى غير بينة كذب وإفك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three traits—chastity, heedlessness, and faith—each make the accusation unjust; together they magnify its wrong and punishment. The wording is general though the occasion was specific.
rows.anchor: أخذ الصفات الثلاث الإحصان والغفلة والإيمان للدلالة على عظم المعصية فإن كلا من الإحصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase on the day tongues and limbs testify modifies the previous verse's promise of great punishment.
rows.anchor: الظرف متعلق بقوله في الآية السابقة { ولهم عذاب عظيم }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds means all evil acts, not only slander; tongues testify about speech sins such as false accusation, lying, and backbiting, while other limbs testify about acts such as theft and malicious walking.
rows.anchor: والمراد بقوله { بما كانوا يعملون } كما يقتضيه إطلاقه مطلق الأعمال السيئة - كما قيل - لا خصوص الرمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each deed is witnessed by the organ that performed it; hands and feet are named because most sins are actions, in keeping with other verses about bodily testimony.
rows.anchor: وبالحقيقة الشاهد على كل فعل هو العضو الذي صدر منه كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, dīn means recompense, as in 'Master of the Day of Judgment'; God pays it fully and completely on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: المراد بالدين الجزاء كما في قوله مالك يوم الدين الفاتحة 4، وتوفية الشيء بذله تاما كاملا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read independently, dīn could instead mean religion or a way of life; this reading describes truths becoming manifest at resurrection and better suits the following clause.
rows.anchor: وأما بالنظر إلى استقلالها في نفسها فمن الممكن أن يراد بالدين ما يرادف الملة وهو سنة الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse illuminates knowledge of God: God is manifest truth, self-evident yet sometimes overlooked; at resurrection people recognize Him when heedlessness lifts.
rows.anchor: فالعلم به تعالى هو ارتفاع الغفلة عنه الذي ربما يعبر عنه بالعلم، وهذا هو الذي يبدو لهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'impure' men and women are unbelievers, whose state of impurity results from being immersed in disbelief; like pairs match by kind.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخبث في الخبيثين والخبيثات وهم غير المؤمنين هو الحال المستقذرة التي يوجبها لهم تلبسهم بالكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matching the impure with the impure does not declare that unbelievers are necessarily involved in lewdness.
rows.anchor: وليسوا بمبرئين عن التلبس بالفحشاء - نعم هذا ليس حكما بالتلبس -.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's wording generally characterizes believing men and women as good; a specific occasion of revelation does not negate that general scope.
rows.anchor: أن الآية عامة بحسب اللفظ تصف المؤمنين والمؤمنات بالطيب ولا ينافي ذلك اختصاص سبب نزولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are legally presumed innocent of accusations until evidence appears and are promised forgiveness and generous provision; these are presumptions honoring faith, unlike the status of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: إنها تدل على كونهم جميعا محكومين شرعا بالبراءة عما يرمون به ما لم تقم عليه بينة.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet drew lots among his wives before travel; she accompanied him on the expedition after the hijab command, carried in a howdah.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة فأقرع بيننا في غزوة غزاها فخرج سهمي فخرجت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: After the army was called to depart, Aisha searched for a broken Zafar-bead necklace; the bearers assumed she was in her howdah, and she stayed behind when they left.
rows.anchor: فإذا عقد لي من جزع ظفار قد انقطع فالتمست عقدي وحبسني ابتغاؤه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha found the necklace after the army had gone, returned to the empty camp, and waited, expecting the party would notice her absence and come back.
rows.anchor: فوجدت عقدي بعد ما استمر الجيش فجئت منازلهم وليس بها داع ولا مجيب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal, traveling behind the army, recognized the sleeping Aisha from before hijab, helped her onto his camel, and led her to the army without speaking to her.
rows.anchor: وكان صفوان بن المعطل السلمي ثم الذكراني من وراء الجيش فأدلج فأصبح عند منزلي فرأى سواد إنسان نائم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says Abdullah ibn Ubayy led the slander; during her month of illness she did not know the rumor, though the Prophet's cooler visits troubled her.
rows.anchor: وكان الذي تولى الإفك عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول فقدمنا المدينة فاشتكيت حين قدمت شهرا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: After recovering, Aisha went with Umm Mistah to relieve themselves at night; Umm Mistah tripped, cursed her son, and then told Aisha about the slander, worsening her illness.
rows.anchor: فعثرت أم مسطح في مرطها فقالت تعس مسطح فقلت لها بئس ما قلت أتسبين رجلا شهد بدرا؟

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha sought confirmation from her parents; her mother said co-wives often speak against a beautiful woman loved by her husband, and Aisha wept through the night.
rows.anchor: يا بنية هو عليك فوالله لقلما كانت أمرأة قط وضيئة عند رجل يحبها ولها ضرائر إلا أكثرن عليها

rows.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
rows.claim: When consulted about separating from his wife, Usama advised the Prophet that he knew her innocence and loved her.
rows.anchor: فأما أسامة فأشار على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالذي يعلم من براءة أهله

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali told the Prophet that God had not constrained him, many other women were available, and he could ask the servant girl for the truth.
rows.anchor: وأما علي بن أبي طالب فقال يا رسول الله لم يضيق الله عليك، والنساء سواها كثيرة وإن تسأل الجارية تصدقك

rows.speaker: بريرة
rows.claim: Asked whether she had seen anything suspicious, Barira said she knew no fault except that the young Aisha sometimes slept and let a household animal eat her dough.
rows.anchor: فدعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بريرة فقال أي بريرة هل رأيت شيئا يريبك؟ قالت بريرة لا والذي بعثك بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet publicly asked who would defend him against Abdullah ibn Ubayy, affirming that he knew only good of his family and the man implicated.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما علمت على أهلى إلا خيرا، ولقد ذكروا رجلا ما علمت عليه إلا خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn Muʿadh offered to kill the offender if he belonged to Aws, and to obey the Prophet if the offender belonged to Khazraj.
rows.anchor: فقام سعد بن معاذ الأنصاري فقال يا رسول الله أنا أعذرك منه إن كان من الأوس

rows.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn ʿUbada rejected Saʿd ibn Muʿadh's offer, overcome by tribal zeal despite previously being a righteous man.
rows.anchor: فقام سعد بن عبادة وهو سيد الخزرج وكان قبل ذلك رجلا صالحا ولكن احتملته الحمية

rows.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
rows.claim: Usayd ibn Hudayr called Saʿd ibn ʿUbada a hypocrite for defending hypocrites and said they would kill the offender; the two clans nearly fought until the Prophet calmed them.
rows.anchor: فقام أسيد بن حضير وهو ابن عم سعد فقال لسعد بن عبادة كذبت لنقتلنه فإنك منافق تجادل عن المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Aisha, her parents, and an Ansari woman wept, the Prophet said that if Aisha was innocent God would clear her, and if she had sinned she should repent; she then asked her father to answer.
rows.anchor: أما بعد يا عائشة إنه بلغني عنك كذا وكذا فإن كنت بريئة فسيبرؤك الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha said her parents had believed the rumor and would not believe her denial, so she cited Jacob's patient endurance and lay down, certain of her innocence.
rows.anchor: إني والله لقد علمت أنكم سمعتم هذا الحديث حتى استقر في أنفسكم وصدقتم به

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Although she expected God to clear her, Aisha did not imagine that revelation would be sent about her, considering her situation too insignificant; she hoped for a dream instead.
rows.anchor: ولكن والله ما كنت أظن أن الله منزل في شأني وحيا يتلى، ولشأني في نفسي كان أحقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says revelation came while the Prophet remained seated; it affected him intensely, and he announced that God had cleared Aisha.
rows.anchor: فلما سري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سري عنه وهو يضحك فكان أول كلمة تكلم بها أن قال أبشري يا عائشة أما الله فقد برأك

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr stopped supporting his poor relative Mistah after the slander, then restored the allowance when the verse urged people of means to forgive; he said he wanted God's forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر والله إني أحب أن يغفر الله لي فرجع إلى مسطح النفقة التي كان ينفق عليه

rows.speaker: زينب بنت جحش
rows.claim: Zaynab testified that she knew only good of Aisha and guarded her senses, though she was Aisha's rival among the Prophet's wives; God protected her through piety.
rows.anchor: فقال يا زينب ماذا علمت أو رأيت؟ فقالت يا رسول الله أحمي سمعي وبصري ما علمت إلا خيرا

rows.speaker: حمنة
rows.claim: Zaynab's sister Hamna fought on her sister's behalf and was among those ruined by the slander.
rows.anchor: وطفقت اختها حمنة تحارب لها فهلكت فيمن هلك من أصحاب الإفك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other routes report the episode from Aisha, Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, Abu al-Yasar, Umm Ruman, and others, with some variation.
rows.anchor: والرواية مروية بطرق اخرى عن عائشة أيضا وعن عمر وابن عباس وأبي هريرة وأبي اليسر الأنصاري وأم رومان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These accounts identify Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Mistah, Hassan ibn Thabit, and Hamna as the slanderers, describing Mistah as an early emigrant and veteran of Badr.
rows.anchor: وفيها أن الذين جاءوا بالإفك عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول ومسطح بن أثاثة وكان بدريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports say the Prophet punished all of them, but gave Abdullah ibn Ubayy two hadd penalties because slandering the Prophet's wife incurred two.
rows.anchor: وفيها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم دعاهم بعد ما نزلت آيات الإفك فحدهم جميعا غير أنه حد عبد الله بن أبي حدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the reports imply the Prophet doubted Aisha, as seen in his changed treatment and in her reported angry replies; he rejects this implication.
rows.anchor: المسلم من سياقها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان في ريب من أمر عائشة بعد تحقق الإفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that prophetic doubt would contradict the verse's rebuke of believers for suspicion: the Prophet, with his station of prophecy and divinely granted protection, most deserved good opinion.
rows.anchor: فمن لوازم الإيمان حسن الظن بالمؤمنين، والنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أحق من يتصف بذلك ويتحرز من سوء الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's sentencing account is contradictory: all four named people were slanderers, yet only Abdullah ibn Ubayy supposedly received two penalties; being the ringleader does not warrant a second hadd.
rows.anchor: وهذا تناقض صريح فإنهم جميعا كانوا قاذفين بلا فرق بينهم. نعم تذكر الروايات أن عبد الله بن أبي كان هو الذي تولى كبره منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one says taking the lead in slander warrants two penalties or that the 'great punishment' in this verse means two hadds.
rows.anchor: ولا أن المراد بالعذاب العظيم في قوله { الذي تولى كبره منهم له عذاب عظيم } هو ثبوت حدين.

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: Al-Qummi says Sunni transmitters report that the slander verses concerned Aisha and the accusation made during the Banu Mustaliq expedition.
rows.anchor: فإن العامة روت أنها نزلت في عائشة وما رميت به في غزوة بني المصطلق من خزاعة

rows.speaker: الخاصة
rows.claim: Al-Qummi contrasts the Imami report that the verses concerned Maria al-Qibtiyya and Aisha's accusation against her.
rows.anchor: وأما الخاصة فإنهم رووا أنها نزلت في مارية القبطية وما رمتها به عائشة.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report transmitted from al-Baqir through Zurara, Aisha says the grieving Prophet's son Ibrahim was only Jurayh's child, so the Prophet sent Ali to kill Jurayh.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول لما هلك إبراهيم بن رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali found that Jurayh had neither male nor female anatomy and reported this; the Prophet told Ali to establish the facts, then praised God for removing harm from the Prophet's household.
rows.anchor: قال لا بل تثبت. قال والذي بعثك بالحق ما له ما للرجال وما له ما للنساء، فقال الحمد لله الذي صرف عنا السوء أهل البيت.
